note: A child-devouring female monster in Greek tradition; later uses often give lamias serpentine features.
short: A child-devouring monster of Greek tradition.

note: Balius, paired with Xanthus: the immortal horses that draw Achilles’s chariot in the Iliad, offspring of the West Wind and the Harpy Podarge.

sources.label: Theoi · Balius and Xanthus, Homer passages

note: Xanthus, paired with Balius: an immortal horse of Achilles. In Iliad 19, Hera grants Xanthus speech, and he foretells Achilles’s death.

sources.label: Theoi · Balius and Xanthus, Homer passages

short: Napoleon’s marshal who became king of Sweden and Norway.
note: Jean-Baptiste Bernadotte (1763–1844), a marshal under Napoleon, later King Charles XIV John of Sweden and Charles III John of Norway.

sources.label: Swedish Royal Court · Karl XIV Johan

note: A dark, dense rye bread. The German name combines pumpern, to break wind, with Nickel, a goblin or devil.

short: The winged horse of Greek mythology.
note: The winged horse of Greek mythology, associated with the Muses. His hoof was said to have struck the Hippocrene spring from Mount Helicon, linking him with poetic inspiration.

short: The American novelist who wrote Grendel.
note: John Gardner, American novelist and scholar of medieval literature, author of Grendel (1971) and The Sunlight Dialogues (1972).

short: The American writer whose papers and library are held at VCU.
note: James Branch Cabell, American writer whose personal library and papers are preserved at Virginia Commonwealth University. His working library contains extensive material on mythology, folklore, and the occult.
